title: fix(plugin-view): route ObjectView's $orderby through the shared sort sink (#4869)
body:
Fixes #4869

`ObjectView`'s non-grid fetch was the last object-bound read site handing an **authored** sort to `$orderby` unlowered. That was not only a structural divergence — it was a live `400 INVALID_SORT`.

## The defect

`ObjectGridSchema.defaultSort` is declared a **single** `{ field, order }` object. `ObjectView` handed it to `$orderby` verbatim, and `QueryParams['$orderby']` declares a `Record<field, direction>` map among its four shapes — so the ObjectStack adapter read that object *as a map* and folded it with `Object.entries`:

```
{ field: 'created', order: 'asc' }   ->   wire   sort=field,order
```

Two columns that do not exist. The server rejects an unreadable sort rather than ignoring it, `ObjectView` swallows the error in its `catch`, and a calendar / kanban / gallery whose only sort was `table.defaultSort` **rendered empty** — while the *same metadata* sorted correctly as a grid, because `ObjectGrid` lowers that pair before using it.

## The change

Per the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-22 (Option A):

- lower the legacy member of the pair **at the read site** — `... || schema.table?.sort || (schema.table?.defaultSort ? [schema.table.defaultSort] : undefined)` — which is verbatim the resolution `ObjectGrid.tsx` already performs for this exact pair, and which `ObjectView`'s own grid path inherits by forwarding both slots;
- route the whole chain through the shared `convertSortToQueryParams` sink, so one normalized shape now reaches `DataSource.find` from every object-bound block.

Precedence is unchanged, and both spellings of the pair keep working.

⛔ **Option B — widening the shared sink to accept a bare `{ field, order }` — was rejected on the merits and is not partially adopted here.** The sink's input slot legitimately also carries `$orderby`'s own map, in which `{ field: 'desc' }` is a valid ordering by a column literally named `field`, so a widened sink would have to guess. A test in this PR guards that rejection: the sink must still refuse the bare object.

⛔ The ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove retirement of `table.defaultSort` (the "C half" of the same ruling) is **not** folded in. It is filed separately as #5861, unassigned, for PM triage.

## ⚠️ Scope check the reviewer should confirm: the ruling named one pin, the pin family is three

The ruling authorises rewriting #5102's `$orderby` assertion at `ObjectView.canonicalTableKeys.test.tsx:348-351` to assert the lowered value. Measured on `origin/main` @ `1d9100eeb`, **that describe block contains three `$orderby` assertions from that same card, all on the same non-grid read path, and all three pin the unlowered value**:

| line (pre-change) | test | was | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 334-337 | `orders by a canonical table.sort` | `[{ field: 'name', order: 'desc' }]` | `{ name: 'desc' }` |
| 339-346 | `prefers table.sort over table.defaultSort` | `[{ field: 'name', order: 'desc' }]` | `{ name: 'desc' }` |
| **348-351** | `still orders by table.defaultSort alone` | `{ field: 'created', order: 'asc' }` | `{ created: 'asc' }` |

Only the third is the line the ruling names. The other two are unavoidable: the ruling directs routing the **whole chain** through the sink, and the chain includes `table.sort`, so no version of Option A leaves them green. I rewrote all three rather than stopping, and flag it here rather than letting it pass silently — **if the narrower reading of the authorisation was intended, this PR needs that call before it leaves draft.**

None of the three was weakened. Each is still an exact `toEqual` on a fully specified map, so both halves of the pair are still pinned as *working* and the precedence between them is still pinned; what changed is the shape they arrive in, which is the defect itself. ⛔ No other pin, assertion, type or exemption was touched.

## The `defaultSort` spelling census the card asked for

The card warned that the sink accepts only a string and a `{ field, order }` array, while the adapter's `serializeOrderBy` also tolerates e.g. a string array (`['-name']`) — so a spelling that works today could become `undefined` after the lowering. Measured, one row per declared source in the chain:

| source | declared shape | reaches the sink as | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `listViews.<name>.sort` | `Array<{ field, order }>` | same | accepted, unchanged semantics |
| `views` prop `.sort` | `Array<{ field, direction }>` | same | direction dropped **before and after** — see below |
| `table.sort` (string) | `string` | same | accepted |
| `table.sort` (array) | `SortConfig[]` | same | accepted |
| `table.defaultSort` | single `{ field, order }` | lowered to a 1-entry array | accepted — **this is the fix** |

**No spelling regressed to `undefined`.** The string-array spelling the card guessed at (`['-name']`) *is* refused by the sink, but nothing in this chain declares it and it has zero authored occurrences in the repo, so it is not a live path. `table.defaultSort` has **zero** authored occurrences in `examples/**`, `apps/**` or `e2e/**` — that measurement is what motivates #5861 and is recorded there.

The one row that needs saying out loud: the `views` prop declares `sort?: Array<{ field, direction }>` while every consumer reads `order`, so the direction is dropped. Measured both ways — unlowered, the adapter's `shorthand(field, undefined)` sent ascending; lowered, the sink's `entry.order === 'desc'` is equally false and sends `asc`. **Same answer before and after**: this change neither repairs nor worsens it. That behaviour is tracked in #5293, which remains open and out of scope here; a pin in `ObjectView.sortSink.test.tsx` records the measurement so whoever takes that card is told this site exists.

## Verification

Green union run **after** the final commit, at `b2779b400`, working tree clean:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-view/src/ \
  packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/sort-query.test.ts \
  packages/data-objectstack/src/orderby-serialization.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
 Test Files  24 passed (24)
      Tests  249 passed (249)
```

(from the repo root — never `pnpm --filter` for vitest here, which silently collects `apps/console`.) The last two paths are untouched by this diff and are included as evidence that the shared sink and the wire serializer were **not** modified.

Other gates, each quoting its own verdict line, all run at `b2779b400`:

- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-view' type-check` -> exit 0, with the script echoed (`> tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) so the filter is proven to have matched. Run **after** `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-view^...' build` (exit 0): the package's tsconfig deliberately drops the source-tree `paths`, so `@object-ui/*` resolves through built `.d.ts`. `packages/core/dist` did not exist in this worktree before that build, so the type-check provably read the `.d.ts` this branch produced, not a cache.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-view' lint` (`eslint .`) -> exit 0, `✖ 247 problems (0 errors, 247 warnings)`. Population read from eslint's own resolution via `--format json`: **37 files, 0 errors**. The new test file contributes 18 warnings, all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` from schema fixtures — the same class and convention as the sibling pin file. This is the package's complete lint job, not a narrowing: `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint` and each package runs `eslint .` in its own directory, and this diff touches exactly one package. The config enables **no** type-aware linting (`languageOptions` sets only `ecmaVersion` and `globals`; no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of any file it does not contain.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` -> `✅ 2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` -> `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 4876 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)`
- `pnpm check:phantom-deps` -> `✅ Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.`
- `pnpm check:self-import` -> `✅ No package names itself inside its own src/.`
- `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` -> `no un-ledgered package emits an extensionless relative specifier`

Not run locally, left to CI, which runs the farm exactly once regardless: `check:published-dist` and `check:eager-closure` both require a full `apps/console` build (the latter reports `No eager-closure report ... This is a broken gauge, not a passing budget` without one).

### Reverse verification

On the real commit, with the mutation confirmed on disk by grepping the changed text — never an editor's exit code — and a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restoring the tree on any exit path.

Predicted **before** running: 13 failures — 10 of 11 in `sortSink`, exactly 3 in `canonicalTableKeys`, and **0** in `namedViewSortArity`.

Observed, source reverted to `origin/main` (on-disk check: injected call site 0, injected lowering 0, old chain 1, bare `$orderby: sort,` 1):

```
Test Files  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
     Tests  13 failed | 29 passed (42)

AssertionError: expected [ 'field', 'order' ] to deeply equal [ 'created' ]
```

That assertion diff **is** the defect: the two non-existent column names the server answered `400 INVALID_SORT` for. Direction as predicted, exactly.

Restore leg: `git diff HEAD --stat` empty, injected text back on disk (call site 1, lowering 1, old chain 0), suite green.

**Legs that do NOT discriminate**, named so the evidence is not overread:

- `ObjectView.namedViewSortArity.test.tsx` — all green in both states. It drives the **grid** path, where `ObjectGrid` does its own lowering; this diff does not touch that path.
- `sends NO $orderby when nothing orderable was authored` — green in both states. With no sort authored the chain is `undefined` either way.
- The two sink assertions inside `keeps the sink STRICT` — green in both states by construction: the sink is unmodified. Only that test's third assertion, which drives the real read site, discriminates.

The wire half of the `400` is not re-proved here: `serializeOrderBy`'s map branch is already pinned in its own home (`data-objectstack/src/orderby-serialization.test.ts` pins `{ name: 'asc', age: 'desc' }` -> `name,-age`), and importing that package into a `plugin-view` test would be a phantom dependency. The read site is what this PR owns, and the assertion above is on the `$orderby` map's **keys**, which is precisely what the server rejected.
